questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Australia because it had long been a place I genuinely wanted to experience. I was excited to explore the unique nature and landscapes and to live in and discover major cities such as Sydney and Melbourne. Academically, Australia was also an excellent fit, as UNSW Sydney is a globally recognised university, particularly strong in law, which made it a highly attractive destination for my exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I could not have wished for a better destination than Australia. Especially Sydney.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a joint orientation upon arrival, and I personally didn’t have many questions. However, it seemed easy for students to access the support they needed, and others appeared to get help quickly – for example with course changes and administrative questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a joint orientation as mentioned.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Australia has a housing crisis, especially in Sydney and Melbourne, and you definitely feel it as an exchange student. I chose the “easy” option and went with a large student accommodation provider, Scape Australia. I stayed at Scape Darling House with a close friend. It was very expensive, but it was hassle-free and I didn’t lack anything: maintenance requests were handled quickly, there was daily food included (a good buffet), and the building had facilities like a gym. My recommendation is to consider this route if you prioritise housing security and a smooth landing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you arrive without housing, be prepared that it can take time to find something—some friends of mine had to move between short-term options at first. In the end, they found really nice places at a significantly lower rent than I paid. So it’s mainly a trade-off: paying more for convenience and certainty from day one versus potentially getting a better and cheaper place, but with a period of uncertainty (and possibly needing short-term accommodation) when you first arrive.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was very frustrating. Once we finally gained access to the course list, I created a detailed Excel sheet to track courses, class times, and assessment formats. However, the offered courses changed multiple times, which made the planning largely useless. In addition, when the “final” course list was released, different students could see different versions depending on when they accessed the system. Because I opened it immediately, I could not see courses that were added later, which made registration unnecessarily difficult.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You are given a list of available courses and then have to submit requests for the courses you want. However, even if a course appears on the list, you can still be rejected from it after applying.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Support was primarily available via email – you could contact the relevant office directly with questions and receive guidance that way.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end, I was able to register for the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient. The process can feel chaotic, but it usually works out in the end. Also, keep in mind that you can change courses at the beginning of the semester if you realise a class is not the right fit, but you need to do it early within the add/drop period.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one undergraduate (BA-level) course and the rest were postgraduate (Master’s-level) courses. As an exchange student, we were only allowed to enrol in one undergraduate course, so the majority of my classes were at Master’s level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was quite different from UCPH. Attendance was expected, and class participation counted towards the final grade. In that sense, it was a bit more “high school-like” compared with the more independent format I am used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of the courses I took. They were relevant, well taught, and overall a very good experience. The Chinese-related course, however, was noticeably more demanding in terms of workload and difficulty, so I would recommend it especially for students who are prepared for a heavier course load and a steeper learning curve.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: One unexpected cost was the extra surcharges added when dining out - many restaurants charge a weekend surcharge and/or a public holiday surcharge. In my experience, these were typically around 5–20%, which can add up over time.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Having a beer or eating out in very touristy areas (e.g., around the Opera House or at Bondi Beach) was cheaper than I expected. Prices were generally similar to other parts of the city, rather than being significantly higher just because it was a tourist hotspot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn’t really make use of the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) during my exchange, so I don’t feel I can assess them properly.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a very wide range of cultural, athletic, and social activities available - honestly something for every interest and preference.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As mentioned earlier, I didn’t personally make use of the non-academic activities, so I can’t recommend specific ones based on my own experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I travelled a lot within Australia during weekends and holidays, which I can highly recommend—it’s a great opportunity to see more of the country. At the same time, I would also suggest making sure to explore the city you live in. I was away so often that I didn’t get to see as much of Sydney as I would have liked.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to adjust to the local culture, as it is quite similar to Europe and feels generally Western in everyday life and social norms.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mainly spent time with other Danish exchange students, so I did not socialise extensively with local students. In several of my classes there were many Chinese students who did not speak English, so while they were very kind, communication was limited. If I were to give a tip, it would be to actively seek out settings where locals are more likely to engag rather than relying on the classroom environment alone.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any particular cultural differences that I found challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated how laid-back Australians are and how relaxed the everyday pace feels. It was a noticeable contrast to a busy routine at home where things often move quickly, and it was genuinely refreshing—it helped me slow down and really unwind.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make the most of it while you’re there—travel, explore, and say yes to experiences.
Try to stay calm even if practical things (course registration, housing, admin) feel frustrating at times; it usually works out in the end.
Enjoy it and be present—the time goes by incredibly fast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was all the experiences I had and the friendships I made. Going on exchange has been the best decision I made during my studies.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Apart from the course registration process, I didn’t experience any major challenges during the exchange. Overall, the transition was smooth and I felt well settled.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
